meta.title: Your dashboard
meta.description: Your unfinished sessions, what to work on next and your accuracy by topic.

dashboard.title: Your dashboard
dashboard.lead: Counted from your own answers. Nothing here predicts a score.
dashboard.unknownExamShowing: That link named an exam we do not offer, so this shows your {exam} practice instead.
dashboard.unknownExam: That link named an exam we do not offer.
dashboard.doesNotTitle: What this page does not do
dashboard.doesNot: It does not predict a score, place you in a percentile, or estimate your chance of admission. Every figure above is a count of your own answers and nothing more.
dashboard.chooseLead: This page then follows the exam you practise, and you can switch between exams here at any time.
dashboard.otherLead: Open another exam here. It does not change the exam you have set as your target.

error.title: Your dashboard could not be loaded
error.body: Something went wrong while reading your practice history. Try again in a moment.

guest.text: As a guest, this browser keeps your practice until {until}. After that, this browser can no longer open it. Create an account to keep it.

unfinished.title: Pick up where you left off
unfinished.question: Question {question} of {questions}
unfinished.clockRuns: The clock keeps running while you are away, as it does in the real exam.

summary.label: Your counts

summary.correctShare: {percent} of everything you have been shown

summary.dueInterval: Missed questions come back after a short interval.
summary.nothingWaiting: Nothing is waiting. Missed questions come back the day after you miss them.

topics.title: Accuracy by topic
topics.lead: Every {exam} topic, including the ones you have not practised. A figure needs at least {min} scored questions; below that the counts are shown instead. Open a topic to see its skills.
topics.figureTooFew: {correct} of {scored} correct · not enough answers for a figure
topics.summary: {skills, plural, one {# skill} other {# skills}} · {reviewed, plural, one {# reviewed question} other {# reviewed questions}} in the bank
topics.caption: Skills in {topic}

noHistory.title: No finished {exam} session yet
noHistory.leadContinuing: Finish the session you started and this page will show your accuracy by topic, what you missed and what is worth practising next, all counted from your own answers.
noHistory.lead: Once you finish a session, this page shows your accuracy by topic, what you missed and what is worth practising next, all counted from your own answers.

emptyBank.title: No reviewed {exam} questions to practise yet
emptyBank.lead: Questions for this exam are still being checked, so there is nothing to start. Only questions that have passed review are ever served.
emptyBank.guide: Read the format and scoring guide

getStarted.title: Take a short session to find your starting point
getStarted.because: You have not answered any questions for this exam yet, so there is nothing to base advice on.

dueReview.title: Revisit {count, plural, one {# question} other {# questions}} you got wrong
dueReview.because: Questions you missed come back after a short interval, which is when reviewing them is worth most.

weakSkill.title: Drill {skill}
weakSkill.because: You have answered {count, plural, one {# question} other {# questions}} tagged to this skill and got {correct} right ({accuracy, number, percent}).

slowSkill.title: Work on pace in {skill}
slowSkill.because: Your accuracy here is {accuracy, number, percent}, but your median time is {seconds} seconds a question. Accuracy is not the problem; speed is.

untouchedDomain.title: Try {topic}
untouchedDomain.because: You have not answered any questions in this topic yet, so there is a blind spot in your picture.

needsMoreData.title: Answer a few more questions before drawing conclusions
needsMoreData.because: {count} of your skills have fewer than {min} answers, which is too few to tell a weakness from a bad day.

broader.label: Practise all of {topic}
broader.because: This skill has {inSkill, plural, one {# reviewed question} other {# reviewed questions}}, so the drill is short; its topic has {inTopic}.

display.timedAnswers: {count, plural, one {# timed answer} other {# timed answers}}

accuracy.label: Accuracy
accuracy.basisRaw: {correct} correct out of {scored} questions shown, across every topic you have practised.
accuracy.basisWeighted: Your accuracy in each topic, weighted by {publisher}'s published share of the exam for that topic, over the {share, number, percent} of the exam you have practised.
accuracy.capNote: Under {usable} answers this reads no better than {band}.
accuracy.basisTooFew: A percentage means something from {min} answers; you have {count}.

pace.label: Pace
pace.basisNoPace: {publisher} does not publish enough for a per-question pace on this exam, so we cannot compare.
pace.basisTooFew: Pace is read from at least {min} answers with a recorded time; you have {count}.
pace.basisUnreliable: Your median time is under {seconds} seconds a question, faster than a question can be read, so it is treated as unreliable timing rather than as speed.
pace.basis: The exam allows about {pace} seconds a question. Your median over {count} timed answers is {median} seconds.

coverage.label: Topic coverage
coverage.basis: Topics of the exam’s own list in which you have answered at least {min} questions.
coverage.touchedOnly: {count, plural, one {# more topic has} other {# more topics have}} fewer answers than that.

volume.label: Evidence
volume.basis: Below {min} answers a percentage is noise; we treat {usable}+ as a usable sample of your own work.

consistency.label: Consistency
consistency.basisTooFew: Consistency compares at least {min} sessions of {answers} or more answers; you have {count}.
consistency.basis: How much your accuracy moves between your last {count} sessions of {answers} or more answers. A wide spread usually means the topic mix is driving the result, not your level.

timing.allUntimed: All of these were answered in untimed practice, with no clock to keep to.
timing.someUntimed: {count} of {total} of these were answered in untimed practice, with no clock to keep to.
timing.missing: {count, plural, one {# answer had no time recorded and is left out.} other {# answers had no time recorded and are left out.}}

overall.insufficient: You have answered {count, plural, one {# question} other {# questions}} for this exam. That is too few to say anything about readiness — answer at least {min} and this becomes meaningful.
overall.weighted: Across the topics you have practised, you are answering {accuracy, number, percent} correctly, weighted the way the exam itself weights its topics. This describes your work on our questions, not a predicted exam score.
overall.unweighted: Across the topics you have practised, you are answering {accuracy, number, percent} correctly. This describes your work on our questions, not a predicted exam score.

projection.methodBocconi: Your accuracy on the questions you attempted ({accuracy, number, percent}) and your rate of leaving questions blank ({omission, number, percent}) applied to the published {items}-question form, scored with Bocconi's published rule: +{correct} correct, {blank} blank, {wrong} wrong.
projection.methodPublished: Your accuracy on the questions you attempted ({accuracy, number, percent}) and your rate of leaving questions blank ({omission, number, percent}) applied to the published {items}-question form, scored with {publisher}'s published rule: +{correct} correct, {blank} blank, {wrong} wrong.
projection.methodConverted: Your accuracy on the questions you attempted ({accuracy, number, percent}) and your rate of leaving questions blank ({omission, number, percent}) applied to the published {items}-question form, scored with {publisher}'s published rule: +{correct} correct, {blank} blank, {wrong} wrong, then converted to the reported scale ({scale}) as published.
projection.assumeDifficulty: It assumes our questions are as hard as the real ones. Their difficulty is our editorial judgement, not calibrated against test-taker data.
projection.assumeConditions: It assumes you answer under the same conditions: {conditions}.
projection.assumeBocconiPenalty: It scores every wrong answer at {wrong} and ignores the larger −0.33 penalty Bocconi applies to some items, so a real form could score slightly lower.
projection.assumeArithmetic: It is arithmetic on your own practice, not a prediction of test day.

target.explanationConverted: {publisher} publishes this exam's scoring in full — a fixed number of questions, each worth the same, a published penalty for a wrong answer and a published conversion to the reported score — so your target can be turned into arithmetic rather than guesswork. The projection below is your own practice accuracy applied to the published form.
target.explanationPenalty: {publisher} publishes this exam's scoring in full — every question is worth the same, and the penalty for a wrong answer is published — so your target can be turned into arithmetic rather than guesswork. The projection below is your own practice accuracy applied to the published form.
target.explanationNone: We cannot tell you whether your practice equals {target}. {publisher} does not publish how a raw score becomes a {scale} score. Anyone who gives you a number for this is estimating. What we can show you is the work itself: how accurate you are in each topic the exam publishes, and whether you are working at its pace.
target.explanationNoneSat: We cannot tell you whether your practice equals {target}. {publisher} does not publish how a raw score becomes a {scale} score, and states that two test takers who answer the same number of questions correctly can receive different section scores. Anyone who gives you a number for this is estimating. What we can show you is the work itself: how accurate you are in each topic the exam publishes, and whether you are working at its pace.

limitations.smallSample: This is based on {count, plural, one {# answer} other {# answers}}, which is a small sample. Treat it as a pointer, not a measurement.
limitations.difficulty: Every figure here comes from your answers to our own questions. Their difficulty is our editorial judgement, not calibrated against test-taker data.
limitations.noPercentiles: We do not report percentiles, and we do not estimate a probability of admission.
limitations.unverified: {count, plural, one {# rule} other {# rules}} of this exam could not be verified from an official source, so some exam-accurate practice is switched off.

suggestions.repeatAll: You have been shown all {all} reviewed questions here, so this repeats them.
suggestions.repeatSome: Only {unseen} of the {all} reviewed questions here are new to you, so this repeats some.

more.title: Answer more questions
more.why: Another {count} answers and the measurements above start to mean something.

review.title: Revisit {count, plural, one {# question} other {# questions}} you missed
review.why: Questions you got wrong or left blank, asked again on purpose. A retry does not count towards the measurements above.

untouched.title: Practise {topic}
untouched.why: You have not answered anything in this topic, so it is a blind spot in everything above.

weak.title: Work on {topic}
weak.why: Your weakest topic with enough answers to act on: {accuracy, number, percent} of {answered}.

timed.title: Practise against the clock
timed.why: Your median time is {ratio, number, ::.00}× the exam's pace. {format} runs to a clock.

suggestionsList.title: Suggestions
suggestionsList.description: What might help next, from the questions available now. These are suggestions, not measurements.
suggestionsList.none: Nothing to suggest right now beyond the sessions in your plan.
suggestionsList.start: Start {count, plural, one {# question} other {# questions}}

reason.tooFew: Too few answers yet to judge.
reason.thinSkill: {skill} has only {count, plural, one {# reviewed question} other {# reviewed questions}}, so its topic is practised.
reason.review: {count, plural, one {# question you missed can be asked again.} other {# questions you missed can be asked again.}} This repeats them on purpose.
reason.mixed: Not enough of your own answers yet to single out a topic.
reason.mixedRevision: You have been shown most of these questions, so this revises them.
reason.revisionAllSeen: You have seen every question here, so this revises ones you have seen.
reason.revisionSomeNew: {count, plural, one {Only # question here is new to you} other {Only # questions here are new to you}}, so this revises ones you have seen.

planParts.completed: Completed with {answered, plural, one {# question} other {# questions}} answered.
planParts.completedOf: Completed with {answered, plural, one {# question} other {# questions}} answered of the {planned} planned.

stateExplained.planned: Scheduled, and its day is not over yet.
stateExplained.completed: You finished a matching session and answered at least {min} of its questions, or all of them if fewer are planned. That is the bar for completing it, not a sign that every question was answered: each one shows how many you did. Opening a session is not enough, and a new-questions session counts only if it was started with new questions only, as Start does.
stateExplained.missed: Its date has ended in every time zone: from 12:00 UTC the next day (13:00 in Italy in winter, 14:00 in summer). Where you are, that is between the midnight after its date and about a day later, never earlier. You can still do it until you adjust your plan, which records it as missed.
stateExplained.skipped: You chose to skip it. It stays in your plan as skipped.

inputs.weeklyHint: Sessions are {minutes} minutes, so this sets how many you get each week.

dateConflict.title: Which is your {exam} date?
dateConflict.lead: We found two, and kept both rather than choose for you.
dateConflict.untilChosen: Until you choose, the date from your goal is used.

notices.planCreated: Your plan is saved. It changes only when you adjust it.
notices.planAdjusted: Your remaining plan is adjusted. Completed, skipped and missed sessions are kept as they were.
notices.planEnded: That plan has ended. Its sessions are kept in your data export.
notices.planExists: You already have a plan for this exam, shown below.
notices.planChanged: Your plan or your practice changed since this preview was made, so nothing was applied. Here is the preview as it is now.
notices.noPlan: That plan is no longer active.
notices.nothingToPlan: There are no reviewed questions to plan for this exam yet.
notices.invalidPlanInput: Nothing was saved: choose a weekly time from the list, and an exam date after today (or none).
notices.sessionSkipped: Session skipped. It stays in your plan as skipped.
notices.sessionClosed: That session is already completed, skipped or recorded as missed.
notices.notEnoughNew: Too few questions you have not seen are left for that session. Adjust your plan to turn it into revision, or skip it.
notices.insufficientContent: Not enough reviewed questions are available for that session right now.
notices.nothingToReview: There are no missed questions to ask again right now: you have answered them correctly since, or they are under review.
notices.rateLimited: Too many sessions were started in a short time. Try again in a few minutes.
notices.dateChosen: Exam date saved. That is now the one date for this exam.

meta.title: Your study plan
meta.description: A dated practice plan built from your own answers and the questions available.

studyPlan.noExamLead: Pick the test you are preparing for, and this page will lay out the next few weeks from the questions available and your own results.

setup.title: Make a plan
setup.dateNotAfterToday: That date is not after today, so the preview uses no exam date.
setup.datePassed: Your exam date, {date}, has passed, so the preview uses none.
setup.dateHintEarlier: Filled in from your earlier study plan, which was not tied to an exam. Clear it if it is not your {exam} date.
setup.dateHint: Your one exam date for this exam, shared with your goal. Leave it empty for a six-week plan.
setup.nothingLead: There are no reviewed questions to plan for {exam} yet.
setup.slotsLeftFree: {planned} of the {slots} sessions your time allows are planned. The rest are left free: there are not enough reviewed {exam} questions to revise a topic more than once a week.

stored.missedTitle: {count, plural, one {# session missed} other {# sessions missed}}
stored.missedLead: You can still do them. Adjusting records them as missed, moves their topics forward and shows you every change before saving.
stored.builtFor: this plan was built for {date}. Adjusting shows what a new schedule would change.
stored.builtForNone: this plan was built for no date. Adjusting shows what a new schedule would change.
stored.endLead: Ending it keeps every session as it is, in your data export, and lets you make a new one.

howItWorks.title: How the plan works
howItWorks.lead: It is built from the reviewed questions available now and your own answers: weakest topics first, then ones you have not tried. It changes only when you adjust it.

adjust.title: Adjust my remaining plan
adjust.dateNotAfterToday: That date is not after today, so this preview uses no exam date.
adjust.datePassed: Your exam date, {date}, has passed, so this preview uses none.

terms.unchangedValue: {count, plural, one {# upcoming session} other {# upcoming sessions}}

adjust.keep: Keep my plan as it is
adjust.nothing: Nothing would change: your plan already matches these inputs.
adjust.dateHint: Your one exam date for this exam. Changing it here changes it for your goal too, once you apply.
adjust.carried: Scheduled first in the new schedule: {sessions}.

meta.title: Progress and readiness
meta.description: How your practice measures against the exam you are preparing for.

progress.chooseLead: Choose the exam you are preparing for, and this view measures your practice against it.
progress.noAnswersLead: This page measures your readiness from questions you have actually answered. Answer some and it becomes meaningful — there is nothing useful we could tell you before that.

report.basedOn: Based on {count, plural, one {# question} other {# questions}} you have answered.

target.title: Your target
target.floorHint: Published by the university as a minimum to be considered — not a competitive score.
target.atOrAbove: On this projection you are at or above your target of {target}.
target.short: On this projection you are {gap} points short of your target of {target}.
target.belowThreshold: On this projection you are below {value}.
target.belowFloor: An application scoring below {floor} is not considered. This is the one number here that is an official requirement rather than a goal you set.
target.howCalculated: How this projection is calculated, and what it assumes
target.noGuessTitle: We will not guess at this
target.officialPractice: Official full-length practice from {publisher} is scored by their own model, so that is where a scaled-score estimate should come from. Use this page for diagnosis — which topics are weak, whether you are working at the exam’s pace — and theirs for score prediction.

signals.title: What we measured
signals.description: Each of these comes from your own answers. The basis for every one is stated, so you can judge whether you agree with it.

gaps.title: Where the ground is weakest
gaps.description: Ordered by what would move your result most: topics you have never attempted first, then your lowest accuracy.
gaps.caption: Your accuracy by topic for the {exam}, weakest first.

targetForm.title: Your goal
targetForm.lead: These two are the only things this page cannot work out for itself.

errors.title: Not saved
errors.outOfRange: A score on this scale runs from {min} to {max}. {score} is outside that.
errors.invalidDate: That is not a real calendar date.
errors.notSaved: That goal could not be saved.

targetForm.scoreHintScale: On the exam's own scale, from {min} to {max}. Leave it empty if you do not have a number in mind yet.
targetForm.scoreHint: On the exam’s own reported scale. Leave it empty if you do not have a number in mind yet.
targetForm.dateHint: Your one date for this exam. Your study plan uses it too, and offers to adjust when it changes.

meta.title: Official practice scores
meta.description: Record the scores you received on official practice tests and follow them over time, kept apart from what UniExamer measures.

officialScores.title: Official practice scores
officialScores.label: User-entered official practice result — not independently verified.
officialScores.lead: Record the scores you received on practice tests published by the test maker itself, exactly as its own tool reported them. We keep them apart from what UniExamer measures: we do not check them with the test maker, convert them to another scale, or predict an official score from your practice here.
officialScores.chooseLead: Choose an exam to record official practice results for.
officialScores.unsupportedTitle: Official practice results can’t be recorded for {exam} yet
officialScores.unsupportedBody: We record a result only on a scale we have checked against the test maker’s own pages, for a practice test the test maker publishes. We have not been able to check one for this exam yet.

latest.title: Latest official practice result
latest.none: You have not recorded an official practice result for {exam} yet.
latest.notComparable: This result is not on the same scale and test version as your target, so the two are not compared.
latest.repeat: This was sitting {n} of this practice test. Having seen the questions before can raise a later score, so read any change with care.

measured.title: Measured in UniExamer
measured.body: Your accuracy, pace and topic coverage from practice here are on the Progress page. They describe your preparation; they are not an estimate of an official score, and they are never mixed with the results on this page.
measured.setTarget: Set a target on the Progress page to see how each result compares with it.

history.title: History
history.separateScales: Results on different test versions or scales are listed separately and never compared.
history.caption: Your recorded results on {version}, newest first.
history.nothingToCompare: No score in common with the previous result
history.confirmDelete: Delete this result? This cannot be undone.
history.deleteFailed: It could not be deleted. Try again.

form.versionHint: Results are only compared with others on the same version and scale.
form.testNameHint: As the test maker names it, for example “Practice Test 4”. It is how repeats of the same test are spotted.
form.overallHint: From {min} to {max}, in steps of {step}. Leave it blank if you did not receive one.
form.noOverall: This test version reports no single overall score. Enter the section scores you received.
form.sectionsHint: Enter only the scores you received and leave the rest blank. Nothing is filled in for you.
form.notesHint: Only you see these: for example, the conditions you took the test in.

errors.title: That result could not be saved
errors.offScale: {field} must be between {min} and {max}, in steps of {step}.
errors.totalMismatch: By the test maker’s published rule, the section scores you entered give an overall score of {expected}. Check the overall score and the sections.
errors.futureDate: The date cannot be in the future.
errors.invalidDate: Enter the date you took the test.
errors.generic: It could not be saved. Check the fields and your connection, then try again.
